html:
Portuguese Ceylon was the coastal part of Sri Lanka held by Portugal, from the arrival of Lourenco de Almeida in about 1505 to the Dutch conquest in 1658.

The Portuguese came for cinnamon, which grew wild in the southwest. They built a fort at Colombo and made the Kingdom of Kotte a client; when its last king died in 1597 they took his lands. They seized the Jaffna Kingdom in 1619 but failed again and again to conquer Kandy in the hills.

Catholic missions made many converts on the coast, and Portuguese surnames such as Perera and Fernando are still common. In 1638 Kandy allied with the Dutch East India Company, which took the forts one by one. Colombo fell in 1656, and Dutch Ceylon began.
sum: Portuguese Ceylon was the coastal part of Sri Lanka held by Portugal, from the arrival of Lourenco de Almeida in about 1505 to the Dutch conquest in 1658.
